stories.title: Wixom Council Backs Zoning Rules to Limit Data Center Noise and Utility Costs
stories.dek: The 4-3 vote advances changes during the 180-day moratorium for a proposed 600,000-square-foot project on 54 acres, after residents raised concerns over power demand, water use, and noise that could raise household bills.

stories.title: Wixom tightens data center rules amid power and water concerns
stories.dek: Wixom is advancing new regulations for data centers as residents express concerns over potential impacts on local power, water resources, and noise levels. The move aims to address community worries while accommodating technological growth. This decision could set a precedent for other Michigan towns facing similar challenges.
stories.source_title: Wixom, Michigan, advances data center rules as worries grow over power, water, and noise - sustainableconstruction-now.com

stories.title: Mason City Council to Resume Debate on Nearby Data Center Proposal and Noise Ordinance
stories.dek: Council members will discuss a proposed hyperscale facility in Vevay Township and potential amendments to a citizen-initiated noise ordinance at Monday's meeting.

stories.title: Mason revives data center tax fight as Jackson eyes personal property rules
stories.dek: Residents in Ingham and Jackson counties are watching new local rules that could decide how much data centers pay in taxes. The debate affects household electric bills and township budgets if big projects move forward. Mason’s return to the issue shows communities are still sorting out who pays for the power these facilities demand.
stories.source_title: What Roth's Watching: Jackson personal property ordinance, data center debate returns to Mason, and more - WKAR

stories.title: AG Nessel demands names behind Michigan's hidden data center contracts
stories.dek: Michigan's attorney general is suing to uncover who signed secret deals for a major data center project. Residents could face higher electric bills and lost tax revenue if the terms stay hidden. The case could set rules for how future projects get approved across the state.
stories.source_title: ‘We don’t even know who signed the contracts’: AG Nessel challenges Michigan’s secret data center deal - thelivingstonpost.com

stories.title: Attorney General Nessel Seeks Court Review of Secret DTE Contracts for Saline Data Center
stories.dek: Michigan AG Dana Nessel asks the Court of Appeals to reopen a contested hearing on DTE Energy contracts for the OpenAI/Oracle hyperscale project, arguing ratepayers deserve transparency on terms and costs.

stories.title: Saline Township brings on ex-cop to steer zoning fights over big projects
stories.dek: The township hired a retired sergeant to manage zoning applications. Residents near Ann Arbor now have a direct contact point when large industrial proposals, including potential data centers, hit the planning desk. The hire signals Saline expects more complex land-use cases in the coming months.
stories.source_title: Saline Township Selects Retired Sergeant for Zoning Role - The Sun Times News

stories.title: Cass County residents pack hall to block data center projects
stories.dek: Save Cass County drew a standing-room crowd to its latest town hall, where neighbors voiced worries over noise, water use and rising electric bills from proposed facilities. The group is pushing local officials to reject or heavily restrict the projects before more land is optioned. Michigan residents 30 miles away could see indirect rate hikes if these sites connect to the same grid.
stories.source_title: Save Cass County holds packed town hall - wndu.com

stories.title: Dowagiac Residents Sue Hyperscale Data Center Over nonstop Noise
stories.dek: Neighbors say a former crypto site now run by Alliance Cloud Services produces a high-pitched whine that forces them indoors and violates the city's new noise limits.

stories.title: Michigan tightens rules on Great Lakes water pulls that data centers need
stories.dek: State officials posted new diversion tracking that directly affects how much water large cooling operations can take from the Great Lakes basin. Data centers under discussion in several counties would need millions of gallons daily, making these rules a key limit on future builds. Michigan residents downstream or near intakes have a direct stake in whether the state grants or blocks those withdrawals.
stories.source_title: Great Lakes water diversions - State of Michigan (.gov)

stories.title: Pere Marquette Township Board Enacts One-Year Data Center Moratorium
stories.dek: The board adopted ordinances imposing a temporary ban on new data center permitting and construction, citing concerns over energy and water demands, with possible extension.

national.title: Data centers advance rapidly as regulators scramble for rules
national.dek: Across the U.S., officials race to impose guardrails on power-hungry facilities while communities push back on incentives and impacts.
